Raw input is not truth. Selected and edited input becomes truth.
This prompt builds the complete Erector system as specified. It has three distinct phases:

The user enters raw goal and raw purpose text. Bhudhi generates 3 refined options for each. The user selects and optionally edits their preferred option. The final edited text becomes the locked source of truth. Nothing proceeds without this step.

The finalized goal and purpose feed a 20-stage validation pipeline powered by Bhudhi (Gemini 2.0 Flash with Google Search for market-facing stages). Each stage produces structured output stored on the validation record. The result is a complete reality check — not a report, a living workspace.

The user sees all 20 stages as interactive cards. They can edit, add, remove, or refresh individual cards. Changes trigger partial recalculation of affected stages only. The user compares original vs updated. When satisfied, they finalize and select an execution path. The finalized package feeds the blueprint.
CRITICAL LAW: Raw input is never the source of truth. Blueprint inherits goal_final and purpose_final. Blueprint does not reinterpret the idea. Blueprint executes the finalized truth.

ALL SCHEMA CHANGES ARE ADDITIVE ONLY. New columns on existing tables must be nullable. No existing column renamed, removed, or given a NOT NULL constraint without a DEFAULT. Migration must be safe to apply on a live database.
DO NOT CHANGE EXISTING BHUDHI CALL INFRASTRUCTURE. Only add new calls and update provider fields as specified. The TriggerRouter, BhudhiLog, fallback chain remain intact.
DO NOT TOUCH: order generation engine, signal engine, condition engine, feedback engine, task generation workers. This build is scoped to the validation and goal refinement layer only.
EXECUTION LANGUAGE THROUGHOUT. No 'Great choice!'. No 'Amazing goal!'. Direct operational language only.

After all 20 stages complete, the user enters the workspace. They do not just read results — they interact with them. Every stage card can be edited, refreshed, or annotated. Changes to some cards trigger recalculation of dependent cards.
Single scrollable page. Each stage is a card. Card layout:
Top: stage number, stage name, source tag (e.g. LIVE SEARCH / AI ANALYSIS), expand/collapse arrow.
Body: stage output in plain language. No technical labels. No score numbers.
Footer: 4 icon buttons — Edit / Add / Remove / Refresh.
Opens the card body as editable text/fields. User changes content directly. On save: marks card as 'user_edited'. Stores original in user_edits array on validation record.
Opens a text input below the card. User types additional context. Appended to stage output. Marked as user_added.
Marks a specific item within a card as removed. Does not delete the stage — removes one bullet or point. Marked as user_removed.
Calls the stage's Bhudhi function again with current inputs + any user edits applied. Replaces stage output. Marks as refreshed. Stores previous version in history.
When certain stages are edited or refreshed, dependent downstream stages must be recalculated. This is a partial recalculation — not a full rerun.

4. Presents the 3 execution path cards for final path selection.
Generated by Stage 19. These replace the previous current/adjusted/alternative naming. Each path has a distinct philosophy, speed, and risk profile.
Slowest. Safest. Proof first. Every assumption tested before the next step. No wasted resources.
Someone building for the first time, someone with limited budget, someone who has failed before and wants certainty before speed.
Balanced speed and learning. MVP first. Ship fast, learn fast, adjust fast. Controlled risk.
Someone who has a clear idea, some experience, moderate resources, and wants to move without being reckless.
Maximum speed. High pressure. Aggressive execution. Accept the risk of moving before everything is proven.
Someone with experience, funding or buffer, high commitment, and willingness to pivot hard if first assumptions are wrong.
